name: FUJINON XF8-16mmF2.8 R LM WR

strengths: Very sharp across the frame, even wide open at f/2.8

Constant f/2.8 aperture at 8mm suits night-sky work
weaknesses: Large and heavy for the X-mount system (805 g)
Bulbous front element accepts no front filters
One of the most expensive X-mount zooms
bestFor: Environmental portraits with dramatic wide-angle perspective

name: FUJINON XF56mmF1.2 R WR
notes: This is the 2022 'R WR' redesign (replacing the 2014 XF56mmF1.2 R and the R APD variant, both now discontinued); task specifically requested this current version. Dimensions (80 x 76mm) are corroborated across retailer/review listings rather than confirmed verbatim on an official spec-page snippet. Launch price is reported here as $999.95 (matching the DPReview announcement headline and Fujifilm's typical US pricing pattern for this lens tier); note that some 2026 retail listings show a higher current price (~$1,199), which likely reflects a post-launch price increase rather than the original MSRP. Unlike the XF23/33/56mm f/1.4 trio, this lens uses a DC motor, not a linear motor.
famousFor: The weather-resistant, redesigned successor to Fujifilm's original 56mm f/1.2, notable as the first X-mount lens with an 11-blade aperture for very smooth bokeh.
strengths: Extremely sharp across the frame at every aperture
11 rounded aperture blades give very smooth, nearly circular bokeh even stopped down
Closer minimum focus distance (0.5 m) than the original XF56mmF1.2 R (0.7 m)
Weather- and dust-sealed construction rated to -10°C
weaknesses: Autofocus uses an older DC motor rather than Fujifilm's linear motor, and is slower and noisier than LM-driven primes
Heavier and pricier than the original XF56mmF1.2 R
bestFor: Portraits with creamy, smooth background blur
Low-light events needing a fast 85mm-equivalent view
Wedding photography wanting shallow depth of field
